honest_caveats_raw10: C1: printenv → echo edge case — `echo "$VAR"` inherits shell-builtin behavior across `sh`/`bash`/`dash`/`busybox-ash`. On Alpine with busybox-ash, `echo -n` flag is interpreted (vs `printenv` which never had this concern); we did not use `-n`, but if any consumer downstream depends on printenv's bare-newline output and the var contains literal backslash-n, semantics differ. Mitigation: all 4 sites are followed by `.trim()`, which strips trailing newline regardless.

C2: timeout 600s may still hit on slower machines — 600s gives ~3x headroom over observed ~200s on M-series. On older macOS Intel hardware (pre-2019) or VMs with throttled CPU, 1.5MB hexa_full.hexa transpile may approach or exceed 600s. Recommendation: if observed 600s exceeds, bump to 1200s or make timeout configurable via env var.

C3: resolve_interp() env var change is a runtime semantic change — was previously hardcoded 4-tier fallback only; now $HEXA_INTERP overrides ALL inferred paths. If a stale or wrong $HEXA_INTERP is set in operator's shell (e.g. carryover from an older build), resolve_interp() will silently use the wrong binary instead of the correct argv0-derived path. This is the 'principle of operator override wins' tradeoff: explicit > inferred. Operators must `unset HEXA_INTERP` if they want the old 4-tier behavior.
